summary.text: Natalie Wells is a Republican candidate for the New Hampshire House of Representatives, Merrimack 8, in the November 3, 2026 general election.
She previously represented Merrimack 25 in the House, serving from 2016 to 2018 and from 2020 to 2022.

paragraphs.text: Wells lives in Warner, New Hampshire, earned a high school diploma from Cranston High School East and an associate degree from Johnson & Wales University, and has worked as a business owner.
In her Ballotpedia survey she described herself as a mother, grandmother, former family business owner and retiree.
Wells served in the House representing Merrimack 25 during 2016-2018, and incumbent David Karrick defeated her in the November 6, 2018 general election.
She won the seat back by defeating Faith Minton in the November 3, 2020 general election, took office on December 2, 2020, and did not run for re-election in 2022.
In 2021 and 2022 she was assigned to the Election Law Committee, serving as clerk.
Wells advanced from the Republican primary for Merrimack 8 in 2024 but was not elected in that year's general election, and she advanced from the primary again on September 8, 2026.
In her survey she listed her key messages as no income or sales tax, protecting parents' rights and school choice, and supporting seniors and veterans.
She listed endorsements from groups including the National League of Taxpayers, Citizens Alliance of NH, Cornerstone Action, the NRA and Executive Councilor Joe Kenney.
